body.statement: Gabriel, Sachs, and Sj\"olander report that, for a two-level instrument with two well-defining exposure levels and one potentially ill-defining level under NPSEM (2.5), the tight valid bounds for the specified target contrast have the same expression as the familiar two-level-IV bounds. They also report that, for a three-level instrument and two well-defining exposure levels under NPSEM (2.2), the tight valid bounds have the same expression as those obtained after allowing a third potentially ill-defining level.

source.locator: Results 1 and 3; references to NPSEMs (2.5) and (2.2)
source.verbatim_statement: For a two-level IV and two well-defining levels of the exposure x and x-prime and one potentially ill-defining level x-m, NPSEM (2.5), the resulting tight and valid bounds for theta-x-prime-x have the same expression as the well-known two-level IV bounds. For a three-level IV and two well-defining levels of the coarsened exposure X, under NPSEM (2.2), the tight and valid bounds have that same expression as those allowing for a third potentially ill-defining level.
